subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and reconcile app-owned LaunchAgent drift after updates, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd/plist state as the UI source of truth, while the report asks for enabled user intent to survive app replacement/update; changing that affects user control, upgrade behavior, and OS-level disables.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd/System Settings state as the source of truth and document that OpenClaw will not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Keep the issue parked until a current-main Sparkle update repro identifies exactly which state flips.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enabled intent and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior Launch at Login persistence fix and macOS app ownership history point most strongly to steipete for this source-of-truth decision.
